review: Whole scan, both overlapping halves, and every line of eight broad enlarged blocks were personally read by the primary reader against C and H. Seventeen focused details at 4–9× and five refinements at 6–8× covered all C doubts, cancelled phrases, subscripts and three diagrams. The left margin was rotated clockwise 24°, then 14° for its upper lines and 29° for the lower clause; the interline insertion and accent were separately inspected at 8×. No context was opened and no statement was mathematically corrected.

decisions.shows: Two detached vertically aligned dots are present, with no letter body. (1510,182,1553,220), 7×.
The word ends in m and a detached point before sur; no final a. Application (236,373,1696,697), 3×.
The opening S is tall and matches the large S of Soit. Application, 3×.
A comma follows the tall h ending; no separate abbreviation point is visible. Application, 3×.
After ou the short ens group has no v/c strokes; des follows it. Application, 3×.
The word ends with a short dotted i before the semicolon; no additional e/s. Application, 3×.

The first word begins with a tall t and long low ou/t join; the next is est, followed by an o-loop and k. The o is small relative to k, favoring lowercase ok, but the case remains doubtful. (545,510,853,568), 6×.
The letter has one upper serif, a straight stem and a lower serif. There is no second bar above a complete I; compare the I in the first diagram. (269,590,312,644), 7×; (664,700,772,853), 6×.
A loop crossed by a long descending stem favors phi, though an overwritten f remains possible. A diagonal crosses the old glyph; it is not a live insertion. (1259,600,1298,655), 7×.

Two short raised strokes precede est and another pair follows it; there are no angle shapes. Margin continuation, 4×.

The lowered glyph has a small upper loop and long S-like descending curve, without a secure detached prime. It resembles xi more closely than a full S prime; the prior readings remain alternatives. (1222,1702,1315,1759), 6×.

decisions.place: right margin extra mark before qui
decisions.shows: After the first comma there is a second separate oblique stroke before qui. Its slash/comma function is unclear, but it is visible ink. Margin continuation, 4× and right crop, 4×.
The final est is readable; its broad horizontal middle may be a crossing or the compressed letter joins. (1400,1701,1465,1745), 7×.
Only an S and descending p precede k; there are no e/c strokes. The left-column connectors have arrowheads; the right column and bottom connector are unheaded. Diagram (38,1625,269,1847), 5×.
Quasi is written in full, followed by c, a descending p, a low c, tall t and a final s curl. (576,1821,712,1886), 6×; bottom (302,1737,1695,2027), 3×.
A clear word-space separates the short pro group from étale. (1200,1824,1336,1884), 6×.
A short m and final s are joined above by a long shallow descending overstroke, not a complete mêmes. Its shape favors a macron but a cursive tilde remains possible. (315,1890,390,1967), 7×.
The tiny mark is a pointed roof with two descending arms; it has neither a comma tail nor two crossing diagonals. (589,1905,618,1942), 9×.
Four separate low points follow décrire. Bottom, 3×.
